name: Adjuvant Abemaciclib + Endocrine Therapy (monarchE)
cyclesNote: 2 years (26 cycles of 28 days) in combination with daily adjuvant endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen).

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026
source.primaryStudy: monarchE: Johnston SRD, et al. J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3987-3998; Harbeck N, et al. Ann Oncol 2021;32:1571-1581
source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K, BINV-M)

biomarkers.note: Requires HR-positive (ER and/or PR positive) and HER2-negative early breast cancer meeting monarchE high-risk criteria: ≥4 pathologically involved lymph nodes, or 1–3 positive lymph nodes with either histologic grade 3 disease or primary tumor size ≥5 cm. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026, BINV-K (3 of 4) and BINV-M (5 of 10) (Category 1, Preferred).

histology: invasive breast carcinoma (ductal/NST, lobular, mixed, micropapillary)
supportiveCare: Diarrhea management: initiate loperamide at the first sign of loose stools (4 mg initially, then 2 mg every 2 hours until diarrhea-free for 12 hours). Increase oral fluids.
Venous thromboembolism (VTE) vigilance: monitor for symptoms of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, particularly if combined with tamoxifen.
Interstitial lung disease (ILD) / pneumonitis: monitor for pulmonary symptoms (cough, dyspnea, hypoxia); hold and evaluate if suspected.
Partner endocrine therapy: give concurrently with an aromatase inhibitor (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane) or tamoxifen for pre/postmenopausal patients (add GnRH agonist for premenopausal).
monitoring: CBC with differential prior to starting, every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, monthly for the next 2 months, then as clinically indicated
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, total bilirubin) prior to starting, every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, monthly for the next 2 months, then as clinically indicated
Monitor for symptoms of thrombosis, diarrhea, and pulmonary toxicity each cycle
clearanceChecks: diarrhea resolution to grade ≤ 1 before restarting

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 diarrhea that does not resolve within 24 hours to grade ≤ 1 despite loperamide
doseModificationRules.text: Hold abemaciclib until resolution to grade ≤ 1; resume at the same dose. For recurrent grade 2 diarrhea or grade 3/4 diarrhea, hold until resolution and reduce by one dose level (150 mg BID -> 100 mg BID -> 50 mg BID; discontinue if unable to tolerate 50 mg BID).
Hold abemaciclib until resolution to grade ≤ 2; resume at same dose. For recurrent grade 3 or any grade 4, resume with dose reduction.

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher ALT/AST elevation (>3x ULN)
doseModificationRules.text: Hold abemaciclib until resolution to baseline or grade 1. Dose reduce for persistent or recurrent grade 2 or any grade 3/4 transaminitis.

drugs.name: Abemaciclib
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 5 of 10. Abemaciclib 150 mg PO twice daily on Days 1 to 28 of 28-day cycle for 2 years (26 cycles), with concurrent endocrine therapy.
